title: Developer Onboard Playbook + Pricing Hooks
body:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic playbook for the Hosted API landing + quickstart funnel that sells Redwood as "developer-first inference you can actually ship with". This is a working doc: experiments, hero copy variants, pricing language drafts and competitor callouts.

Audience
- Primary: Software engineers and ML engineers evaluating an API for production inference (fast iteration, predictable latency, cost controls).
- Secondary: Platform/infra leads who influence procurement (considers SLAs, dedicated capacity, private deployment).

Core developer-first value props (short hooks for hero / H1/H2)
- "From prototype to production: an API that’t surprise you on latency or cost."  
- "Ship LLM features with predictable performance and dev ergonomics."  
- "Real engineering controls: batching, caching, quantization suggestions, and transparent per-token economics."

Messaging pillars (used to build bullets on landing + quickstart)
1) Fast time-to-value: SDK-first, example apps, <5-minutes to first completion. Include runnable samples (node/python) that create a chat and an embeddings flow.
2) Predictable latency & SLOs: emphasize benchmarks, latency percentiles, and dedicated pools for predictable throughput. Short line: "When tail latency matters, choose predictable endpoints."
3) Cost control & observability: token-level breakdown, per-route cost, recommendations to cut unit cost (batching, cache, quantization). Call out Redwood Optimize as a follow-up flow.
4) Multi-mode deployment: start hosted, scale to Dedicated/Private without rewriting code. "Same API, same telemetry, different infra."
5) Developer ergonomics: streaming, tool/function calling, structured outputs and first-class SDKs. Provide a one-file starter that implements streaming + cancelation.

Quickstart angles to A/B test on page & email sequences
- "Run a chat in 3 lines" (code-snippet hero) + CTA "Try with free credits"
- "Migrate an existing OpenAI flow in 6 steps" (migration checklist for engineers)
- "Measure your latency and cost in under 10 minutes" (landing -> telemetry quick demo + calculator)
- "Playground -> API" (interactive playground that exports code)

Suggested hero copy variations (short)
- Variant A: "An API engineers trust for production LLMs" (emphasize reliability)
- Variant B: "Ship LLM features faster, pay less per useful token" (time + cost)
- Variant C: "Predictable performance. Transparent pricing. Dev-first SDKs." (balanced)

Pricing language drafts (voice: clear, engineer-trustworthy, avoid vague markers)
- Core: "Pay-as-you-go for hosted inference: per-input token + per-output token pricing, per-embedding unit for vectors."
- Free tier: "Starter tier includes X free embedding units and Y free generation tokens per month." (experiment with concrete limits vs. % off)
- Enterprise clarity: "Reserved/Dedicated capacity: flat committed monthly fee for guaranteed throughput and SLA-backed latency targets. Contact sales for private deployment pricing and on-prem packaging."
- Cost controls copy: "Turn on autoscaling, batching, or prefix caching to reduce per-token cost; our Optimize tool will show estimated savings before you change settings."
- Comparison snippet for devs: "Transparent token accounting vs opaque per-request pricing — you can see exactly where you spend."

Competitor callouts (notes for sales enablement & landing copy differentiation)
- Cloud-managed endpoints (large cloud providers): call out: "Good for generic managed compute, but inconsistent tail latency and costly per-request variability. Redwood: predictable SLOs + smarter batching for lower unit cost on real workloads."
- LLM API providers (simplicity-first): call out: "We match their simplicity but add production controls (dedicated capacity, private deployment, token-level observability)."
- Self-hosted inference vendors: call out: "Self-hosting gives control but large ops burden. Redwood: keep operational simplicity with optional Dedicated/Private modes."

Open questions / things to validate (TODO)
- Exact free tier numbers (eng/finance input) - experiment: 1M gen tokens + 10k embed units or 30-day $200 credit.
- Best hero CTA phrasing for conversion: “Try free credits” vs “Start a runnable sample”. A/B test both.
- Which benchmark artifacts do we publish on landing? Need small artifact set: 1) 256-token chat p95 across models/regions, 2) batching cost-savings example.
- Migration checklist: write 6-step doc to convert an OpenAI chat completion flow to Redwood endpoints (PR to docs).

Sales-enablement snippets (one-liners for outreach)
- "If your app needs consistent tail latency and lower per-token costs at scale, Redwood gives you both without rewriting your codebase."
- "Use our SDKs to get from PoC to SLA-backed production in weeks, not quarters."

Tracking & experiments (suggested metrics)
- Quickstart funnel conversion: hero CTA -> run sample -> obtain API key -> generate 1st token. Track dropoff at each step.
- Time-to-first-successful-inference (median) measured by telemetry snippets from SDK. Aim <5 minutes for new users.
- Pricing page interactions: clicks to pricing calculator and downloads of committed-dedicated PDF.

Notes / Links we should attach to the canonical doc (placeholders)
- Confluence: gtm/hosted-api-landing (copy deck + benchmark assets)
- JIRA: GTM-472 (quickstart implementation work)

Working next steps (owner suggestions)
- Draft 3 hero variations + wire copy for calculator (Owner: Maya).
- Engineering: provide two runnable starter repos (node/python) and an embedding example that outputs an L2 similarity table (Owner: Ethan).
- Finance / Legal: finalize free tier boundaries and enterprise contract language (Owner: Priya).

Notes to self: keep voice straightforward and engineer-respectful. Avoid marketing fluff. Include concrete knobs engineers can act on (batch size, cache TTL, quantization level).

End of doc (working draft).
